round1.offer:
ROAST:
You sell a $40 lamp at a 20% discount to people who already wanted it, then wonder why there is no money left. A coupon is not an offer. Right now the only reason to buy today is a code half of TikTok already knows.

Your AOV is $44, so most people buy one lamp and leave. Every order pays a $19 toll to Meta and you keep about five cents of net profit per sale. Traffic is fine; the value on the page is what is broken.

FIXES:
1. Kill GLOW20 and build a bundle: lamp + second colour head + 12-month replacement warranty + "room glow-up" lighting guide at $59. -- AOV from $44 toward $55-60 with no extra ad cost
2. Add a named guarantee: "Love the glow in 30 days or we refund and you keep the lamp." -- cuts purchase risk; test refund rate before rolling out
3. Add a 2-pack at $69 ("one for you, one to gift") with a real deadline tied to stock. -- lifts units per order and gives urgency that isn't a fake timer

SCORE: 4/10
ONE-LINER: Stop discounting the lamp and start stacking value around it.
round1.copy:
ROAST:
"Transform your room into a sunset paradise" is the headline every sunset lamp has run since 2021. Your market is past the stage where a big promise works; they have seen this exact claim a thousand times. Sparkle emojis do not make it new.

The ad names the product's job but never the buyer's feeling: the empty, flat-white rented bedroom that looks nothing like the rooms they save on Pinterest. Talk to that. And "the viral lamp everyone is talking about" admits you are a copy.

FIXES:
1. Lead with identification, not a claim: "Your rental has landlord-white walls. Here is the 40-dollar fix that makes it look like your saved Pinterest board." -- matches a market that has heard every lamp promise
2. Give it a mechanism and a name: the 4-head "Golden Hour Halo" that is why it looks warmer than cheap single-lens lamps. -- a new reason to believe for a sophisticated market
3. Replace "Limited time only" with a concrete proof line: number of reviews, a before/after photo, or a creator quote. -- swaps hype for believability

SCORE: 3/10
ONE-LINER: Your market has heard your headline; give them a reason it's different this time.
round1.profit:
ROAST:
Congratulations, you built a $42,000-a-month business that pays its owner fifty dollars. After refunds, product, shipping, ads and overheads, net profit is roughly 0.1%. Call it what it is: a very busy hobby with a Shopify plan.

And the plan is to scale ads to $30k? Spending more to grow a 0.1% margin just makes the hole bigger, faster. Revenue is vanity here; the bank balance is the truth.

FIXES:
1. Open a separate Profit account today and move 1% of every deposit into it, then step up a point each quarter. -- forces the business to work around profit instead of leftovers
2. Cap ad spend at the level that keeps contribution margin at or above 20% (about $15k/month at today's numbers) until AOV improves. -- stops buying revenue at a loss
3. Attack the 7% refund rate: add a set-up video in the box and a pre-shipping "what to expect" email. -- each point of refunds saved is about $420 a month back

SCORE: 2/10
ONE-LINER: Pay yourself first, or the lamp is the only thing in this business that glows.
round1.creative:
ROAST:
Six ads, all the same shot: lamp on a wall with trending audio. That's one angle filmed six times. Advantage+ can only pick between options you give it, and you gave it six copies of the same idea.

No face, no hook in the first second, no problem shown. Your 2.27 MER against a 1.58 break-even ROAS says the ads still work while carrying a weak offer. Before you add $12k of spend, add new angles.

FIXES:
1. Ship 3 new angles in 2 weeks: a "rental glow-up" before/after, a creator-style "things that made my room look expensive" list, and a gift angle for Q4. -- new angles, not new edits, unlock scale
2. Put a hook in the first second (text on screen + a face or a hand flicking it on) and judge every ad by 3-second hook rate, aim for 30%+. -- finds winners in days, not weeks
3. Hold spend flat and run a weekly creative test budget of 15-20% of spend, scaling only ads beating 2.5x on 7-day click ROAS. -- scales winners without burning cash

SCORE: 4/10
ONE-LINER: More angles first, more budget second.

round2.offer:
STANCE: AMEND
TARGET: The Profit Keeper
TAKE: Right that scaling a 0.1% margin is madness, but capping spend alone just shrinks a broken machine. Fix the offer first: the $59 bundle lifts margin per order, and then the spend cap can rise instead of fall.
round2.copy:
STANCE: ENDORSE
TARGET: The Creative Strategist
TAKE: New angles beat new edits, agreed. The rental glow-up angle is exactly the identification hook this market needs, and it should carry the Golden Hour Halo name so the creative and the copy say the same thing.
round2.profit:
STANCE: AMEND
TARGET: The Offer Doctor
TAKE: The bundle is smart, but a 'keep the lamp' guarantee on a 7% refund rate could get expensive. Launch the bundle first, fix the refunds with the set-up video, then test the bolder guarantee on 20% of traffic.
round2.creative:
STANCE: ENDORSE
TARGET: The Offer Doctor
TAKE: A $59 bundle gives me something to sell besides a coupon. Each new angle can end on the bundle, and a higher AOV lowers the ROAS bar we need to hit before scaling.

verdict.headline: A real product with demand, trapped behind a coupon offer, a recycled headline and a 0.1% net margin.

priorities.action: Replace GLOW20 with a $59 lamp + extra head + warranty bundle and a $69 2-pack
Open a Profit account and move 1% of every deposit; hold ad spend near $15k until contribution margin is 20%+
Shoot 3 new angles (rental glow-up, room-upgrade list, gift) with a first-second hook; test at 15-20% of spend
Rewrite ads and PDP around the rental identification hook and the named Golden Hour Halo mechanism
Add an in-box set-up video and a pre-shipping expectations email to cut the 7% refund rate

watch_out.quote: A coupon is not an offer.
Your market has heard your headline; give them a reason it's different this time.
Spending more to grow a 0.1% margin just makes the hole bigger, faster.
That's one angle filmed six times.

verdict.closing_line: Fix the offer, then the angles, then the budget, in that order, or the only thing scaling is the loss.
